newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FORECAST-Czech Feb trade gap seen at CCr. 14.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Czech Feb trade gap seen at CCr. 14.5 bln.

text.p: The Czech February trade deficit should nearly double to 14.5 billion crowns from 7.84 billion in the same month of 1996, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Friday.
Czech February trade figures are to be released by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Monday.
Most economists surveyed said they expect the widening trend of the trade deficit seen over the past few months to continue.

"Even though the crown weakened at the time, I think we may see at least the same deficit as in January -- 13.6 billion crowns -- if not slightly more," said Boris Gomez, an analyst at ING Barings in Prague.
The crown weakened some three percentage points against its dollar/mark basket midpoint between the end of January and mid-February after hitting a high of +5.51 percent against the midpoint.

Vladimir Kriedl, an economist at investment bank Patria Finance added that while the crown has weakened, it will affect both import and export totals in February, thus having little impact on the balance.

"If the crown is strong, both imports and exports as expressed in crown terms are nominally lower, so I expect both export and import growth (in February) to be lower but this will not affect the deficit," he said.
The widening trade deficit -- which has consistently shown the rate of import growth exceeding export growth -- has become one of a number of growing problems for the Czech economy.

December's deficit, a nearly 18 billion crown shortfall, helped push the full year 1996 trade deficit to a record 160.3 billion crowns and the CSU has forecast the gap to widen to between 211-219 billion crowns.
A CSU survey of importers and exporters on the trade deficit for the first quarter of 1997 should nearly double, year-on-year, to 45 billion crowns.

The foreign exchange and money markets are expected to show little reaction to the figures -- as the worsening Czech trade balance has been long built into crown rates -- as long as the results do not vary greatly from the estimates.
Analysts say the trade balance has been hurt by a downturn in western European economies. The effects of a recovery in demand have yet to make an impact on Czech exports.

Czech crown dealers said the trade figures could have a significant impact on the currency, though it will be somewhat muted since stronger than expected 1996 GDP figures calmed fears on the foreign exchange markets of an imminent cut in interest rates.
The crown strengthened in Friday afternoon trading to 0.98 percent above its dollar/mark basket midpoint, after opening at about +0.15 percent.
